selected_sources.title: Sufficiency and Approximate Sufficiency
selected_sources.role: Primary source for approximate sufficiency/deficiency and its decision-theoretic interpretation.
native_points: Approximation of statistical experiments is defined relative to experiments indexed by the same parameter set and randomizations/decision procedures.
Deficiency quantifies approximate simulation of one experiment by another; risk comparison for bounded losses is the operational decision-theoretic interpretation.
Normalization conventions for total-variation/deficiency constants must be declared rather than silently assumed.

selected_sources.title: Equivalent Comparisons of Experiments
selected_sources.role: Exact decision-comparison baseline for information ordering of experiments.
native_points: Comparison is stated in terms of attainable risk across decision problems.
Exact comparison/equivalence is weaker or stronger depending on the decision class; Blackwell also introduced k-decision comparisons.

selected_sources.title: Comparison of Statistical Experiments
selected_sources.venue: Encyclopedia of Mathematics and its Applications 36
selected_sources.role: Authoritative monograph connecting risk, deficiency, sufficiency, randomization, distance, ordering, equivalence, and convergence.
native_points: Deficiency is a quantitative information-comparison device, not a free-standing universal metric.
The theory explicitly relates deficiency to decision theory and randomization.

selected_sources.title: Le cam theory on the comparison of statistical models
selected_sources.role: Accessible expository cross-check of Le Cam distance and decision-risk interpretation; not used as the foundational authority.
native_points: Reviews Le Cam distance, deficiency, and classical tools for bounding them.
Provides an accessible modern statement linking small deficiency to uniformly small increases in bounded-loss risk.

selected_sources.title: Coding Theorems for a Discrete Source With a Fidelity Criterion
native_points: A nonnegative distortion matrix is supplied as part of the problem.
Average distortion is probability-weighted over source/reproduction pairs.
A tolerable distortion level is an explicit constraint, and the rate-distortion function depends on the source and chosen distortion measure.

selected_sources.title: The Information Bottleneck Method
selected_sources.venue: Proceedings of the 37th Annual Allerton Conference on Communication, Control, and Computing
native_points: Compression is defined relative to a relevance variable/joint distribution rather than by a universal distortion.
The constrained optimization trades compression against preserved relevant information.
The formulation is described as a rate-distortion generalization in which an effective distortion arises from joint statistics.

selected_sources.title: Approximation Metrics for Discrete and Continuous Systems
native_points: Approximate language inclusion/simulation/bisimulation are quantified by a hierarchy of pseudometrics.
The pseudometrics are built for metric transition systems and depend on the observation/system structure.
Established exact relationships are recovered as zero sections within the stated framework.

selected_sources.title: Convexity, Classification, and Risk Bounds
selected_sources.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
native_points: Surrogate loss improves computational tractability but changes the statistical objective.
The paper gives a quantitative relationship between surrogate risk and 0-1 target risk.
Nontrivial target-risk control requires a calibration/Fisher-consistency condition on the chosen surrogate loss.

selected_sources.title: Nonlinear Multiobjective Optimization
selected_sources.venue: International Series in Operations Research & Management Science 12
native_points: Multiple objectives may be conflicting or incommensurable, so single-objective methods are insufficient without additional structure.
The literature distinguishes no-preference, a posteriori, a priori, and interactive methods, reflecting different roles for preference information.
A Pareto/efficient set is not automatically a unique most-preferred solution.

selected_sources.title: On scalarizing functions in multiobjective optimization
selected_sources.role: Primary comparison of scalarization choices and their relationship to supplied preference information.
native_points: Different scalarizing functions encode different approaches and can have different theoretical/numerical behavior.
Preference/reference information is part of many scalarized formulations; scalarization is not a preference-free canonical collapse.

selected_sources.title: Computational and Statistical Tradeoffs via Convex Relaxation
selected_sources.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
selected_sources.role: Primary example showing explicit tradeoffs between computational and statistical resources.
native_points: Inference quality is studied under bounded computational resources such as time or space.
Algorithms can be ordered by both computational and statistical efficiency.
The paper derives concrete runtime-versus-data tradeoffs rather than collapsing the two resources by default.

selected_sources.title: Model Selection and the Principle of Minimum Description Length
selected_sources.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
selected_sources.role: Primary/authoritative statistical treatment of description length as a model-selection complexity criterion.
native_points: MDL compares models through coding/description complexity of data and model representations.
Description length is a distinct complexity notion and is not identified with runtime, memory, sample count, or communication cost.

cross_family_observations: No selected native source establishes a universal approximation metric, loss, tolerance, aggregation rule, or scalar cost.

Approximation structures differ materially across families: deficiency/risk over randomizations, probability-weighted distortion, system pseudometrics, calibrated surrogate/target risks, Pareto/preference orders, and heterogeneous resource tradeoffs.
Zero numerical discrepancy recovers an exact relation only under family-specific separation/equivalence conditions; it is not a generic consequence of calling a field 'loss' or 'metric'.
Cost and adequacy are distinct in the selected sources; computational, statistical, and description-complexity resources are not identified as one natural scalar.
